main_body: Grey stove body (rows ~8-31) with a lighter grey top plate at rows 9-12, a dark-framed fire opening with flame at rows 18-25, and a tall grey front panel below
top_band: light grey-blue band rows 9-12 with two small dark dots, then a lighter 1-2 row strip at rows 12-13; it reads as a flat plate/rail rather than a surface seen from above
evidence: Reading a column down the middle: dark outline at row 8, a light grey band at rows 9-11 with dots, a lighter strip at rows 12-13, then a dark gap and a large flat grey front panel from row 14 to 31. The upper band looks like a vertical plate or a control panel face, not a horizontal top. Only 1-2 rows can be called a top edge, which is a rim. The firebox is a dark inset square with a flame, painted face-on. The whole stove is a straight front elevation with a hat band, so it fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The front panel is a large flat grey area with only a thin lighter left edge and a few shades. The outline is a dark, almost neutral grey-black frame around the whole piece. Only the flame has any colour variation. Compared with the stall and well references, which carry many ramps, tile scallops and grain, this stove has much less information per tile and looks like a sticker.
